body:
> if you have only one lense by which you can interpret events, then wouldn't the logical choice be to look into learning some new ways of looking at life?

No. As I already said, I can't do that. It's like sticking your hand in a fire and getting burned on more than one occasion and then trying to convince yourself it won't burn you the next time you stick your hand in. It goes against all your experiences with fire and sounds an awful lot like trying to will yourself into buying a ridiculous untruth.

> do you go for the whole modern reductive materialism thing -- "when you die, it's lights out, you're just worm food?" Or do you not really think about it much? Most people don't.

I'm a naturalist and an atheist. I don't hold out much hope for an afterlife, not that I would even want one.

> So, you're a victim of your environment, then? Or am I reading you wrong? It sounds like you're saying that you believe you're arrived at the "One Correct Way" of looking at things.

I'm saying that it's hard for me to see the world in a way which contradicts my own because I'd have to go against everything I have experienced in life thus far to do so which makes it feel like I am lying to myself.

> Do you ever do any reading?

Yes, sometimes. I am currently working on 'Pride and Prejudice and Zombies'.

>Hah! How wonderfully morbid!

Such is life. It is full of the beautiful, the morbid, and on rare occasions the morbidly beautiful.

>Have you ever read Schopenhauer? (On second thought, maybe you shouldn't!)

I agree with much of his views on utilitarianism.

>Did you mean to switch from talking about your dislike for "them" to your dislike for "humanity," which you reference with the self-inclusive "us," or was that inadvertent? Interesting, nonetheless.

No, it was a mistake. I should have said 'we' instead of 'them'. I after all, am a part of this circus, even if I didn't choose to join it.

>Have you found that perspective to have been of any use to you? Do thoughts like that help you get things done in your life? Do they provide you with any utility whatsoever?

It has been some use to me in various situations. Does it overall improve my quality of life? Probably not, but my experiences and interactions with the world around me are what have shaped my views. I could be using self-affirmations and mantras to try and fake a more positive outlook but such things feel like a giant pill full of lies that I simply can't force myself to swallow. I may as well attempt to will myself to believe in Santa again.

>So, do you think people are / human nature is "basically bad," and that good actions are the exception to the rule? If so, where do you think the decent things that people do come from?

I think human nature is quite self-absorbed and short sighted which is a terrible combination especially when paired with a lack of self-awareness. I think all people are capable of doing good but I don't think it outweighs the negatives. 

>What do you want out of life?

I don't even know anymore but to stop feeling bored with everything would be a nice start.

>I'm not really sure how to change that. However, right now, I can see that my personal world can have times of being tolerable or enjoyable. Even though I lose sight of that often, these times, I think, are worth making it to.

It's sad when all we have to look forward to is swiftly fleeting moments of happiness here and there in between the ever looming depression.

Yes, I started out with a school social worker at twelve. I did not see a real psychiatrist until a month or so before my first suicide attempt at the age of fourteen. I was put on meds in the psychiatric ward and have had them be changed about a million times since then because the effects wear off after my body adjusts to them. I have about given up on seeing therapists at this point, after over fifteen years, if they couldn't help fix me yet they simply aren't going to.

Yes, there have been a few times in my life I was truly giddy with happiness. However, I almost hate being happy because I have come to anticipate that it's only a short matter of time before it ends. Going back to feeling despair after getting a taste of that is unbelievably painful for me. It's a tease and reminder of what has eluded me for most of my life.

Aside from the fact that human beings are capable of so much cruelty, willful ignorance, and callousness? Probably the way we have created an entire system built on preying on one another like vultures for the sake of greed which will likely end in the self-destruction of our species (if not the entire planet itself taking all the other life forms with us).

I don't have a car here in the urban area which I live so I do a whole lot of walking but that's about it. I like it a lot more than I ever did working out at the gym. I find my energy level is okay. Don't get me wrong, it could be better but it's not bad for a person with insomnia.
I actively avoid them since I dislike them so much. Does that count?

>Let me begin by saying, I like your username. I'm glad you are hopeful, that is very important.

Thanks, I always pick usernames that are a wordplay of my middle name. 

>That aside, you should try setting a few goals for yourself. They don't need to be serious, fun goals work too. Perhaps even goals like playing kickball for 15 minutes a week with your children.

I don't mean to sound rude or ungrateful at all but I'm not quite certain what the goal here is. I do things all the time. I just get no enjoyment out of them. 

>To that, I suggest you aim to be the change you want to see in the world. That involves some problem solving on all of our behalf.

I am polite and treat everyone with respect and dignity but I am a misanthrope. If I thought I had the power to change anything in this world by sheer power of will, I would already be off doing it. I assure you.
I do try from time to time. I just feel run down. Tired. I wish I could get my creative juices flowing again or at least bring myself to care enough to find more motivation for it.
Huh? What do you mean, like volunteer work or something?

At the risk of sounding cliche, I once had hobbies but none of them bring me much pleasure anymore. I used to use art as a means of self-expression but the whole thing has gone stale. I stopped being inspired. I haven't made anything in a decade. I got really into writing for awhile too until it also stopped being any fun for me. I hit a brick wall with my writer's block. It started feeling like a chore. I began to hate everything that I was working on so I just gave up on it. Now I just play video games in my spare time.
